The Gmail sign-in code investigation happened in [Build the first-run flow on top of the credits branch](#local_cea7b182-1404-4ee3-afa3-e87cbafe7c2d). It wasn't a session of its own: you raised it partway through that session on 2026-11-03, while working on the first-run flow in the `first-run-flow-f7be35` worktree. That session is the earliest one to contain the test emails. Several later "btw" side chats from the same worktree hold copies of it.

That session ended without an answer. The question was why Gmail on the web shows a "Code Requested" card with a "Copy code" button for OpenRouter's code email but not for JusPrin's "Your JusPrin sign-in code" email.

- **What was tried:** four test emails went from staging to `k+probe@obico.io`, each changing one thing. One put the code in the subject, one used "verification code" wording, one added an HTML part, and one did all three. None of them showed the card.
- **What the search found:** Google publishes no rule for which senders get the card.
- **Where it stopped:** you said "Stop here." One possible cause was never checked. `support@obico.io` is one of your own addresses, so Gmail labels every JusPrin email as sent mail in your inbox, and that might hide the card. The test left is to send the code email to a mailbox where `support@obico.io` isn't your address.
Do one more try by including the code in the email title. Send a few test emails first.

input.ask: Which inbox should the test emails go to?

content.text:
I haven't sent anything yet, because the code-in-the-subject version has already been tried once. On 2026-11-03 the earlier session sent "314159 is your JusPrin sign-in code" to `k+probe@obico.io`. Gmail showed no "Copy code" card for it, or for the other three versions sent with it.

I've found how that session sent the emails. It ran a small Django script on the staging web server (the `tsdweb-stg` pod) and sent them from support@obico.io, the same address that sends the real sign-in code. I can send new ones the same way in under a minute.

**Decision needed: which inbox should the test emails go to?** In your k@obico.io mailbox, support@obico.io is one of your own addresses. Because of that, Gmail files every JusPrin email there as sent mail. It may also treat the email as one you wrote yourself and skip the code card, though nothing we found online confirms or rules that out. While that stays possible, a repeat send to `k+probe@obico.io` can't tell us much: no card would mean what it meant last time. An inbox where support@obico.io is not one of your addresses fixes this. A personal Gmail account works, or a Google Workspace inbox at a domain other than obico.io. Sending there costs nothing extra. The only catch is that you have to open each email in that inbox and tell me whether the card shows. My pick is an outside Gmail address you can check. Which address should I send them to?

Once you give me an address, I'll send three or four versions. Each will have the code in the subject, and they'll differ only in the subject wording, for example "314159 is your JusPrin sign-in code" and "314159 is your verification code", which is OpenRouter's exact pattern. Then you tell me which ones show the card.

I sent four test emails from the staging server to `k+probe@obico.io`, and all four are in that inbox now, unread. Each one has the code in the subject. They come from "Obi The Owl <support@obico.io>", the same sender as the real sign-in email, and differ only in the subject wording and whether there's an HTML version:

| # | Subject | Format |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 582917 is your JusPrin sign-in code | plain text |
| 2 | 603418 is your verification code | plain text |
| 3 | 749263 is your verification code | plain text + HTML, like OpenRouter's |
| 4 | Your JusPrin sign-in code: 815034 | plain text |

Email 3 is the closest copy of OpenRouter's email, which does get the card. If even that one shows nothing, the email's format probably isn't the cause. The likelier explanation would then be that Gmail sees support@obico.io as one of your own addresses and skips the card. Gmail did mark all four as sent mail again, as it does for every JusPrin email in this mailbox.

Please open each one in Gmail on the web and tell me which, if any, show the card.
